record.paper_title: Open problems in theory of nuclear open quantum systems
record.original_question: How can the Gamow Shell Model, which has mostly been applied to nuclear-structure calculations, be fully extended to reaction problems using a coupled-channel scattering formulation while preserving its treatment of bound states, resonances, and many-body scattering continua?

evidence.quote: This model, formulated in the Rigged Hilbert Space and using a complete Berggren ensemble, is a generalization of the nuclear ISM for a description of bound states, resonances, and many-body scattering continuum.
So far, most applications of the GSM have addressed nuclear structure phenomena.
Further progress can only be achieved if the method could be fully extended to reaction problems.
This can be achieved by the coupled-channel formulation of the scattering problem.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Setup. Consider an A-body nuclear system modeled as an open quantum system in the Berggren single-particle basis, which combines bound, narrow-resonance (Gamow) and complex-energy non-resonant continuum states and provides a complete one-body basis in a Rigged Hilbert Space. The Gamow Shell Model (GSM) is the configuration-interaction many-body theory built on Slater determinants of such Berggren orbitals; it simultaneously describes bound states, resonances, and many-body scattering continua of the A-body Hamiltonian H.

Problem. Provide a fully developed extension of the Gamow Shell Model from a structure model to a reaction model, formulated as follows.

(a) Define a complete set of binary mass partitions (channels) c = {(A_T, A_P); (α_T J_T, α_P J_P); ℓ s J}, where the target |α_T J_T⟩ and projectile |α_P J_P⟩ are GSM eigenstates of the corresponding sub-Hamiltonians, and ℓ, s, J are the relative orbital, channel-spin, and total angular momenta.

(b) Construct properly antisymmetrized channel basis states |(c, r)⟩ in the relative coordinate r between target and projectile centers of mass (e.g., via cluster/Jacobi or cluster-orbital relative coordinates), so that the A-body wavefunction admits the resonating-group-type decomposition
   |Ψ^J⟩ = Σ_c ∫ dr r^2 (u_c(r)/r) Â |(c, r)⟩,
with Â the inter-cluster antisymmetrizer.

(c) Derive, from the GSM many-body Hamiltonian H, the resulting non-local coupled-channel integro-differential equations for the radial channel functions u_c(r),
   Σ_{c'} ∫ dr' [H_{cc'}(r, r') − E N_{cc'}(r, r')] u_{c'}(r') = 0,
including microscopic direct kernels H_{cc'}, exchange/non-orthogonality (norm) kernels N_{cc'}, and the proper Coulomb asymptotics; impose scattering boundary conditions for u_c(r) compatible with the Berggren completeness so that bound states, resonances, and the many-body scattering continuum of H are all preserved.

(d) Show that the resulting framework yields, in a unified manner, the structure observables (energies and widths of bound and resonant A-body states) and the reaction observables (S-matrix, elastic, inelastic, transfer, and radiative-capture cross sections) for low-energy nuclear reactions, while remaining fully consistent with the open-quantum-system character of the underlying GSM.

Question. Carry out this construction explicitly, establishing the coupled-channel scattering formulation of the Gamow Shell Model that simultaneously preserves its description of bound states, resonances, and many-body scattering continua, and that is applicable to general nuclear reactions.
artifact.category_tag: Open quantum systems and nuclear reaction theory
artifact.status_search_result: Substantial progress has been made: the coupled-channel Gamow Shell Model (GSM-CC) has been formulated and applied to elastic/inelastic scattering, proton/neutron radiative capture (e.g., 7Be(p,γ)8B, 7Li(n,γ)8Li, 17F(p,γ)18Ne), and more recently to transfer reactions such as 40Ca(d,p). A monograph titled "Gamow Shell Model: The Unified Theory of Nuclear Structure and Reactions" summarizes the framework. Hence the program proposed is partially solved/under active development, with extensions to broader reaction classes still ongoing.
